title: Zandvoort hosts the final edition of the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix
seoTitle: Zandvoort Hosts Final Dutch GP: Russell & Norris Shine
subtitle: George Russell wins the sprint race and Lando Norris secures pole position at the circuit
excerpt: Zandvoort takes center stage with the sprint race and qualifying for the final edition of the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Zandvoort is in the international sports spotlight due to the Formula 1 track activities, which include the sprint race and the definition of the starting grid. The weekend marks the final edition of the Dutch Grand Prix at the circuit, drawing the attention of fans and teams to this leg of the season.

The sprint race in Zandvoort

The twenty-four-lap short race was won by Mercedes' George Russell, who converted his pole position into a triumph. The British driver maintained the lead until crossing the finish line, just as rain began to fall at the circuit. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished in second place after overtaking Lando Norris on lap eighteen, while Norris completed the podium in third place for McLaren.

Intense grid battle and qualifying

In the activities that set the grid, Lando Norris secured pole position for the main race. The qualifying session featured extremely close lap times among the top competitors, with Russell securing second place and championship leader Kimi Antonelli securing third for Mercedes. Max Verstappen claimed the provisional third position on the grid during the decisive phases at his home circuit.

Farewell to the traditional circuit

The current leg marks the circuit's farewell to the category's calendar, sparking reactions from drivers and fans about the track's characteristics. Drivers highlighted the challenging layout and the closeness of the fans, with the traditional orange crowd supporting Max Verstappen. Low profitability for promoters led to the end of Formula 1's run at the venue following its return in twenty twenty-one.

Expectations for the main race

With qualifying and the sprint concluded, teams are adjusting their cars for the official race start. Weather conditions and tire wear remain central factors for the competitors' strategies as the grid lines up for the final official race at the Dutch track.

With information from Formula 1, The Guardian.
